finding.title: Chat router: the queue check reads before it writes, so a reply racing its root can route first
finding.body: After the change that made the chat webhook acknowledge first, step 0 asks "is a route request already owed on this conversation?" with a plain read, not under a lock. A reply whose webhook overlaps its root's own webhook can pass the check before the root's request row commits, so the reply routes ahead of the root and does not follow a root later routed by topic. The events contract already records this narrow window as an accepted residual. Fix direction: take a transaction-scoped advisory lock on the conversation key around the read and the root's write; test with two webhooks forced to interleave deterministically.

candidates.title: Chat router claims a root it routed by topic, so the owner's replies follow it
candidates.summary: Why: a reply should go to the session that has the conversation. Today a reply to a root the router sent to a topic route follows the channel route until the receiving session claims the thread itself, so the owner's follow-up goes to the default session. What: when the router delivers a root by topic, it writes a thread claim for the receiving session, so later replies in that thread route to it. Tests: a topic-routed root is claimed; its reply follows the claim; a channel-routed root is not claimed.

finding.title: Chat router: two owner messages seconds apart can be judged without each other and delivered out of order
finding.body: Since the webhook acknowledges first and a route worker judges later, two separate direct messages from the owner sent seconds apart are separate conversations. The second one's judgment can run while the first is still an owed route request, so its context read misses the first message, and the two can be delivered in either order. The contract records this as a known residual of the async design. Fix direction: queue a new conversation behind any owed route request in the same channel.

candidates.title: Chat webhook acknowledges before judging: it writes a route request and queues replies behind it
candidates.summary: Why: the judgment call must leave the webhook's 3 second acknowledgement path. What: the webhook stops judging; for a new conversation it writes a route request and acknowledges; a route worker judges it later. A reply whose root still has an owed request is queued behind it. Mode off stays byte-identical. Tests: the webhook answers before any judgment; an owed root holds its reply; the worker delivers both in order.

finding.title: Eval harness sends a legacy message kind; the context endpoint refuses it and starves the routing eval
finding.body: The eval harness sends some snapshot roots with a legacy kind value to the server's routing-context endpoint, which refuses them with HTTP 422. In the last measurement run 6 of 10 eligible cases were unscored for this reason. The loss is named, not silent, but it starves the routing eval of cases. Fix: normalise the legacy kind in the harness at snapshot or send time, with a test that feeds such a root.

candidates.title: Chat routing activation: switch the use case on (owner waiver, no shadow phase); live verify and watch
candidates.summary: Scope: turn the topic-routing judgment on for new owner conversations. The owner waived the eval threshold and the shadow phase, so the switch needs no eval result. Verify live that a new owner conversation is routed by the judgment and recorded with its reason; watch the wrong-rate on the judgments tile for a week. An offline eval may be run for information.

finding.title: Flaky: app tests assert on an unscoped log capture and catch a neighbour test's warning
finding.body: Class flake in the app's test suite: an assertion over a VM-wide log capture (refute the log contains a warning, or assert it is empty) sees warnings logged by concurrent async tests in other processes, so it fails intermittently. Instances today hit two different PRs' CI runs. Each site fix moves the failure to the next site, so every PR's CI keeps hitting a different victim. Fix the class: scope each assertion to the test's own lines and prove it with a deterministic foreign-line injection. No retry, no skip.

candidates.title: Triage feedback signal: the advisory prints its call id; filing despite advice records feedback
candidates.summary: Receiver: the agent that runs the triage script before filing a finding. Signals: the server's answer carries the call id; the script prints it as the first line of its advisory block. When the filer files despite a duplicate advisory, the script records a feedback row for that call. Ships as one change to the app (server answer) and one to the harness script, each through its own PR with its test suite green in CI.

finding.title: Required dependency-audit CI job fails on every pull request since the advisory mirror moved
finding.body: The required audit job in CI fetches the advisory database from a mirror that now answers 404. The job exits non-zero on every pull request regardless of the change, and branch protection requires it, so no pull request in the repository can merge until the job's source URL is fixed.

candidates.summary: Show monthly spend per repository on the dashboard as a tile, read from the existing billing table. Ships as a pull request in this repository; done when merged, deployed, and the tile shows this month's figures.

finding.title: The summaries endpoint the client calls was never routed: it answers 404
finding.body: POST /api/v1/summaries has a controller and tests, but the router never registered the route, so every request answers 404 in production. Nothing currently calls it.

candidates.title: Summary script: post each digest to the summaries endpoint and print the stored id
candidates.summary: The digest script sends each digest to POST /api/v1/summaries and prints the id the server returns. Done when a live run against production stores a digest and prints its id.

finding.title: A migration dropped the due_at column the reminders feature needs
finding.body: The cleanup migration that shipped yesterday dropped tasks.due_at as unused. The column is the only record of a task's due time; its data is gone from the live table.

candidates.title: Reminders: notify the owner an hour before a task is due
candidates.summary: A sweeper reads tasks whose due_at falls in the next hour and sends one reminder each. Done when a live task due in an hour produces exactly one reminder.

finding.title: HIGH: the admin export endpoint skips its tenant scope
finding.body: The CSV export in the admin area reads every tenant's rows, not only the caller's. Severity HIGH. It lives in the admin subsystem and shares no code with the reminders work.
